content:
alex: heads-up — last night's nightly-eval run spiked timeouts for the int8 quantized model on pool `eval-quant-2`. timeout rate went from ~8% to ~40% between 03:00-04:00 UTC. looks infra-y not model-only. :eyes:
chris: do we have a specific job id / logs? is it a single worker or spread?
alex: job=nightly-evals-2026-03-19-03, failing across ~6/16 workers in that pool. attaching the most common stack-ish log snippet below:
```
[2026-03-19T03:12:07Z] worker=12 sample loop: start inference
[2026-03-19T03:14:07Z] worker=12 quantized::gemm fallback path triggered (long-tail)
[2026-03-19T03:14:07Z] worker=12 sample_timeout after 120s (deadline exceeded)
[2026-03-19T03:14:07Z] worker=12 closing session, pid=24391
```
alex: interestingly the ones that failed are all on hosts with `node-image:v2026-03-10`
maria: I rolled kernel->5.15.89 on that image last week (security backport). no config changes beyond that. ops didn't touch cpusets.
julia: quantized path is very sensitive to microsecond scheduling jitter — if BLAS falls back to scalar path we can see big tail latency. any chance CPU freq scaling kicked in?
chris: good call — I can see from monitoring that CPU freq on those hosts dropped to ~800MHz for a ~15m window at 03:05 UTC. that's the exact window for the spike.
alex: that would explain it. quantized GEMM sometimes needs burst GHz; if it can't, fallback plus heavy mmap/IO could blow past the 120s test timebox.
maria: why would freq drop during nightly run? not much user load. we usually have `ondemand` governor active. we did flip the default governor to `powersave` in the security image build to reduce thermal noise in long runs (was meant for infra-only), maybe that landed on these nodes accidentally.
julia: repro idea: run the same sampling workload under `performance` vs `powersave` on a test host and compare p50/p99. if p99 collapses under powersave that's our smoking gun.
chris: I'll repro on one host now. quick command we used to stress: 
```bash
# run harness sample subset
python eval_harness/run.py --model rdl-int8-test --prompt-set smoke-100 --workers 4 --timeout 120
cpupower frequency-info # check governor
```
chris: confirmed locally: with `powersave` p50 ~90ms tokens, p99 ~2.8s. with `performance` p99 ~320ms. under `powersave` the small GEMM fallback showed 4-6x slower kernels, sometimes stalling the thread for seconds.
alex: that maps to the observed timeouts once multiple tokens queue up.
maria: ok this is an infra regression — accidental governor flip on node-image. I'll push a fix to image build to set governor to `ondemand` (or `performance` for eval pool). ops will rollout to `eval-quant-2` first.
julia: short-term mitigation: can we set an env override in the nightly-eval job to set `GOVERNOR=performance` or run `cpupower frequency-set -g performance` in job startup?
chris: yes, we can add a startup hook in the eval job spec. I'll add a safe fallback: if we detect governor != performance, set it and log change. CI-bot: starting a dry-run patch to nightly job with governor override — patch id gh/infra/2739.
ci-bot: dry-run applied to staging-nightly-evals-1, triggered job run (link: https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/gh/infra/2739).
ci-bot: run completed, timeout rate down to 5% on staging.
maria: ops action: revert accidental powersave default, mark node-image v2026-03-10 as deprecated, new build v2026-03-19 will force `ondemand` by default for eval pools. rollout scheduled 03:30 UTC.
alex: can we also add a test to the node-image presubmit that asserts cpufreq governor not `powersave`? small YAML change.
maria: yes will add.
julia: also add a microbench to nightly smoke that runs a 10s quantized GEMM microkernel and rejects image if p99 > threshold. prevents regression slipping in.
chris: owners and tasks: maria: image rebuild + presubmit test; chris: job startup governor fix + rollout; julia: add microbench; alex: check if any other pools got the image and ping product owners.
alex: thanks y'all. re: follow-up, I'll post a brief note for customer-facing incidents channel in case any external customers used Dedicated nodes with that image. :thumbsup: :bug: 
maria: +1, will coordinate.
ci-bot: tagging this thread as resolved in tracker: INFR-7123, linked PRs: gh/ops/334, gh/infra/2739.
alex: closing the loop — nightly-eval spike root cause = accidental `powersave` governor on specific node-image causing long-tail quantized kernel slowdowns -> timeouts. mitigations deployed to staging and rollout scheduled.
chris: leaving monitoring alerts muted for 1h during rollout, will re-enable after verification.
julia: thanks everyone, nice triage. :clap:
